definition: ETAP-3 is a proprietary linguistic processing system focusing on English and Russian.
details: It was developed in Moscow, Russia at the Institute for Information Transmission Problems (ru:Институт проблем передачи информации им. А. А. Харкевича РАН). It is a rule-based system which uses the Meaning-Text Theory as its theoretical foundation. At present, there are several applications of ETAP-3, such as a machine translation tool, a converter of the Universal Networking Language, an interactive learning tool for Russian language learners and a syntactically annotated corpus of Russian language. Demo versions of some of these tools are available online.

explainer.lead: ETAP-3 is a proprietary, rule-based system for processing English and Russian, developed in Moscow at the Institute for Information Transmission Problems. It turns one linguistic framework into several practical tools, including machine translation and resources for learning and studying Russian.

tiers.eli5: ETAP-3 is like a very detailed language instruction book that a computer can follow. Instead of learning languages by reading millions of examples, it uses rules about how words and meanings fit together. Those rules help it translate, teach Russian, and label the structure of Russian sentences.
tiers.practitioner: ETAP-3 is applied through task-specific tools for machine translation, Universal Networking Language conversion, interactive Russian learning, and syntactically annotated Russian text; some have online demos. Its rule-based design and English–Russian focus are central constraints, so it should not be treated as a general multilingual component. Proprietary licensing may also affect access and integration.
tiers.paperLevel: ETAP-3 can be summarized as: English/Russian linguistic input -> rule-based processing grounded in Meaning-Text Theory -> task-specific linguistic output. The output may be a translation, a UNL conversion, learning support, or syntactic annotation, depending on the application. Its stated scope is English and Russian, and its processing is rule-based rather than a claim of broad language coverage.

explainer.example: In an illustrative translation task, the Russian sentence “Я читаю книгу” could be supplied to the machine translation application to produce an English rendering such as “I am reading a book.” The important point is that ETAP-3 performs this task through its rule-based linguistic system, not by substituting isolated words alone.

explainer.intuition: ETAP-3 approaches language through explicit linguistic rules rather than treating translation or analysis as simple word replacement. Meaning-Text Theory supplies the foundation for connecting linguistic meaning with its expression in text.
howItWorks: Receive English or Russian linguistic input.
Use Meaning-Text Theory as the framework connecting meaning and text.
Pass the result to an application such as translation, UNL conversion, language learning, or corpus annotation.
explainer.whyItMatters: ETAP-3 shows how a single theory-driven linguistic system can support both practical applications and language resources. Its annotated Russian corpus and interactive learner extend its role beyond translation alone.
misconceptions: It is not just a machine translator; it has several distinct applications.
Its focus is English and Russian, not unrestricted multilingual processing.
Online demos do not make ETAP-3 open source; it is proprietary.
